Subject: Regional binding and tenant purge acceptance plan - Acme Health

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our dedicated deployment onboarding we need explicit confirmation of two things before legal signs the contract: 1) how you will ensure our tenant data is anchored to the US west region (no replication out of region except for transient backups), and 2) an auditable purge workflow that we can use during decommissioning or upon DSAR/erasure requests.

Specifically, can you provide:
- A short description of the technical controls that enforce regional binding (cluster placement, network controls, replication config).
- The retention and backup deletion timeline and where snapshots are stored.
- The purge verification artifacts we will receive (log entries, snapshot IDs, signed manifest).
- An estimated timeline to execute a tenant purge and produce evidence.

Our security and DPO folks prefer concrete artifacts we can attach to the procurement questionnaire. If you have a runbook or checklist we can review that would help speed approval.

Thanks,
Pascal Thompson
Head of Cloud Security
Acme Health

Pascal — thanks, good questions. Quick response while I loop infra and contracts.

Short answers up front:
- Regional binding: Dedicated cluster will be provisioned in US-West (region tag us-west-2) with tenancy scoped network ACLs; no cross-region replication enabled by default.
- Backups: Automated snapshots are stored in an account-scoped S3 bucket with region enforcement; incremental snapshots kept for 14 days by default for the Dedicated plan (adjustable per SOW).
- Purge verification: We provide a signed purge manifest, snapshot deletion records, and a condensed audit log extract showing the purge run and checksum mismatches.
- Timeline: We can schedule a formal tenant purge window; typical end-to-end is 72 hours to run and validate, plus up to 5 business days for producing signed artifacts depending on cross-team approvals.

I attached our working wipe runbook and a network topology diagram for reference. Ben — can you confirm the exact artifacts and the verification checklist we will hand to Acme? Aditya — I'll need a short contract clause we can add around the purge acceptance criteria and SLA impact.

Next steps: Ben to provide technical confirmation and example artifact samples; Aditya to propose contract language; I will collate and send a single package for Pascal's legal team.

Best,

Thanks Vanessa — adding technical detail for Acme's security team. Apologies for the long note, wanted to be explicit so you have artifacts to attach.

1) Region locking / isolation-
- Dedicated clusters are provisioned in a single AZ cluster inside us-west-2. The orchestration layer sets node anti-affinity outside the cluster but all nodes remain in the same region tag.
- Object storage for snapshots uses an account bucket with a region constraint policy (S3:PutObject condition aws:RequestedRegion = us-west-2). Cross-region replication is disabled at the account level for the bucket used for Dedicated customers unless the customer explicitly requests scoped DR (we will not enable without a signed SOW).
- Network: We enforce VPC firewalls and subnet routing such that egress to other region endpoints is blocked; NAT gateways and endpoints are region-specific.

2) Snapshot / backup lifecycle-
- Automated incremental snapshots: retained 14 days by default; full snapshots monthly retained 90 days (configurable).
- Snapshot storage location: us-west-2 S3 bucket, encryption with customer-managed KMS key (optional). Deletion of snapshots triggers an internal audit event and a background compaction job; we record snapshot IDs and deletion timestamps.

3) Purge workflow & verification artifacts-
- Purge steps: quiesce tenant traffic -> export small retention metadata -> run KV/volume zeroing and overwrite (3-pass overwrite for block stores) -> delete snapshots -> revoke tenant KMS key (optional) -> run consistency checks.
- Evidence we produce: signed purge_manifest.csv (tenant id, resource ids, snapshot ids, timestamp, operator id), audit_log_extract.txt (timestamps of each step), s3_delete_records.jsonl (S3 delete marker entries and object version ids) and a brief verification report signed by our infra lead.
- For additional assurance we can provide a hash diff of a post-purge storage probe showing no reachable tenant objects.

4) Timeline & runbook-
- Dry run: 1 business day (non-destructive verification).
- Production purge: scheduling required; typical window 72 hours to perform and validate all steps if no unexpected blockers.
- Artifact delivery: we aim to hand over the signed artifacts within 48–120 hours after completion depending on legal sign-offs.

Attachments: sample_purge_manifest_ACME.csv (redacted), purge_evidence_checklist.xlsx (internal).

If you want, we can include a short lived test purge on a staging tenant to demonstrate the artifact set (no production data involved).

— Ben Carter
Principal Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Thanks Ben — that level of detail is great. From a contracting perspective I propose the following short addendum you can share with legal:

- Region binding: Redwood will provision Dedicated resources in us-west-2 and will not enable cross-region replication without mutual written agreement (customer-initiated DR is an opt-in SOW item).
- Purge acceptance: Redwood will execute tenant purge per the attached runbook and will provide the signed purge_manifest.csv, audit_log_extract.txt, and S3 delete records. Customer acceptance is considered complete when the signed manifest and audit extract are delivered and the verification report notes zero remaining tenant objects.
- SLA: Purge execution and artifact delivery timelines are excluded from the standard uptime SLA; any committed schedule will be captured in the SOW.

I've attached a Docusign-ready SOW template with the acceptance clause filled in; Vanessa, please send to Pascal once you and security confirm the artifact set. Pascal — if this works for Acme's legal we can add it to the Master Services Agreement.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
